[[File:Fussball-Bundesliga Deutschland 2008-09.png|thumb|Fussball-Bundesliga Deutschland 2008-09]]
The '''2008–09 Bundesliga''' was the 46th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] league. The season began on 15 August 2008 with a 2–2 draw between defending champions [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] and [[Hamburger SV]] and ended with the last matches on 23 May 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se12/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 2008/2009 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> [[VfL Wolfsburg]] secured their first [[List of German football champions|national title]] in the last match after a 5–1 win at home against [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]].

==Changes from 2007–08==

===Structural changes===
Starting with the 2008–09 season, two-legged relegation playoffs between the third last team of the [[Bundesliga]] and the third team of the [[2. Bundesliga]] at the end of the regular season were re-introduced.

Due to the restructuring of European competitions, the third-placed team qualified for the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League]], entering in a separate qualifying round for non-champions. The fourth-placed team and the winner of the [[2008–09 DFB-Pokal]] qualified for the [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League]] play-off round; the fifth-placed team qualified for the third qualifying round. The sixth-placed team did not qualify for any European competitions because the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]] was not continued after its [[2008 UEFA Intertoto Cup|final edition in 2008]].

===Promotion and relegation===
[[1. FC Nürnberg]], [[F.C. Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]] and [[MSV Duisburg]] finished the [[2007–08 Bundesliga|2007–08 season]] in 16th through 18th place, respectively, and therefore were relegated to the [[2008–09 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]]. They were replaced by the top three teams of [[2007–08 2. Bundesliga]]: [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]] and [[1. FC Köln]], respectively.

==Promotion/relegation play-offs==
[[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]], as the 16th-placed team, faced third-placed [[2008–09 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[1. FC Nürnberg]] for a two-legged playoff. Nürnberg won both matches on an [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregated]] score of 5–0 and thus secured promotion to the [[2009–10 Bundesliga]], while Cottbus were relegated to the [[2009–10 2. Bundesliga]].

After Energie were relegated, no teams from the former East Germany played in the Bundesliga until [[RB Leipzig]] earned promotion to the Bundesliga for [[2016–17 Bundesliga|2016–17]].
